ncc_references.relationship: Primary prescriptive context for residential masonry wall, pier, component and weatherproofing object classes.

objects.name: masonry wall assembly
objects.definition: A wall built from masonry units joined with mortar, together with the leaves, cavities, ties, supports, movement joints and moisture-control components required by its particular arrangement.
functions: Enclose or divide building space
Carry loads where designed as loadbearing masonry
Resist weather, fire or impact as required by the selected wall system

cad.pattern: Continuous wall runs divided at openings and movement joints
cad.placement: On a designed footing, slab edge, shelf angle or other structural support
cad.start: Wall end, return, intersection or movement joint
cad.end: Wall end, return, intersection or movement joint
cad.opening: Interrupted and supported around doors, windows and other openings
cad.load: May be loadbearing, non-loadbearing or veneer according to the wall arrangement

notes: This is a family-level assembly. A drawing tool must select the wall arrangement before generating leaves, cavities, ties and supports.

objects.name: masonry veneer wall
objects.definition: A wall arrangement in which a single outer masonry leaf is tied to a separate structural frame and generally carries its own weight while the frame carries the building loads.
functions: Provide an external masonry skin
Resist face loads through ties to the structural backing
Protect the framed wall behind from direct weather exposure

ncc_references.relationship: Primary prescriptive object and arrangement context for masonry veneer.

cad.pattern: Outer leaf following the framed external wall perimeter
cad.placement: Outside a timber or steel structural wall frame with a drained cavity
cad.start: Veneer termination, return or articulation joint
cad.end: Veneer termination, return or articulation joint
cad.opening: Spans openings with lintels and is flashed and drained around them
cad.load: Self-supporting vertically; tied to the structural frame for face-load restraint

notes: The veneer is not the primary roof- or floor-loadbearing wall merely because it is made from masonry.

objects.name: brick veneer wall
objects.definition: A masonry veneer wall whose outer leaf is constructed predominantly from brick-sized masonry units.
functions: Provide a durable external brick finish
Transfer face loads through veneer ties
Drain incidental moisture through the cavity and flashing system

ncc_references.relationship: Brick is a common masonry-unit implementation of the masonry veneer provisions.

cad.pattern: Bonded brick courses along external framed walls
cad.placement: Outside the structural frame with a cavity
cad.opening: Lintelled, flashed and drained around wall openings
cad.load: Veneer role rather than primary building-frame role

objects.name: reverse masonry veneer wall
objects.definition: A framed wall arrangement with a masonry leaf on the room side of the insulated frame so the masonry mass is exposed to the interior rather than used as the outer weather skin.
functions: Provide internal thermal mass
Form a durable internal masonry surface
Work with the external framed and clad weather envelope

cad.pattern: Internal masonry leaf aligned with selected external framed walls
cad.placement: Inside an insulated structural frame and external weatherproof cladding system
cad.opening: Detailed around openings as part of the complete framed envelope
cad.load: Usually an internal masonry mass and finish; structural role must be specified

notes: This common sustainable-design arrangement is supported by Your Home, but it is not treated as a synonym for the NCC Part 5.2 external masonry veneer arrangement.

objects.name: cavity masonry wall
objects.definition: A masonry wall formed by two masonry leaves separated by a cavity and connected with wall ties so the leaves act together for face-load restraint while remaining physically separated.
functions: Form a two-leaf masonry enclosure
Limit moisture transfer from the outer leaf to the inner leaf
Transfer face loads between leaves through cavity ties

ncc_references.relationship: Primary prescriptive context for cavity masonry walls.

cad.pattern: Parallel inner and outer leaves connected by repeated ties
cad.placement: On continuous structural support appropriate to both leaves
cad.start: Return, cross wall or wall termination
cad.end: Return, cross wall or wall termination
cad.opening: Both leaves are supported and moisture-detailed around openings
cad.load: One or both leaves may be loadbearing according to the design

notes: Cavity masonry is broader than double brick because either leaf can use other masonry units.

objects.name: double brick wall
objects.definition: A cavity masonry wall in which the inner and outer leaves are constructed predominantly from brick-sized masonry units.
functions: Provide a durable two-leaf masonry enclosure
Use the cavity to interrupt moisture transfer
Provide high-mass wall construction

ncc_references.relationship: Double brick is a common brick implementation of cavity masonry.

cad.pattern: Two parallel bonded brick leaves
cad.placement: On support sized for both leaves
cad.opening: Lintelled and moisture-detailed through both leaves
cad.load: Inner leaf commonly carries building loads; project design governs

objects.name: single-leaf masonry wall
objects.definition: A masonry wall only one unit-leaf thick, without a separate masonry leaf or framed structural backing forming the same wall assembly.
functions: Form an internal or external wall with one masonry leaf
Carry vertical or face loads where designed
Provide mass, separation or a finished masonry surface

ncc_references.relationship: Primary prescriptive context for unreinforced single-leaf masonry.

cad.pattern: One bonded masonry leaf following the wall path
cad.placement: On a continuous designed support
cad.start: Return wall, engaged pier, intersection or termination
cad.end: Return wall, engaged pier, intersection or termination
cad.opening: Supported over openings and restrained beside them
cad.load: May be loadbearing or non-loadbearing according to the design

notes: Single leaf describes wall arrangement; it does not mean the individual units are solid rather than cored or hollow.

objects.name: reinforced masonry wall
objects.definition: A masonry wall strengthened by steel reinforcement placed in mortar joints or in grouted unit cores so the reinforcement and masonry act as a designed structural assembly.
functions: Carry structural actions through reinforced masonry
Increase bending, shear or tension capacity where designed
Integrate steel reinforcement with grouted masonry cells or joints

ncc_references.relationship: Reinforced masonry lies outside the Housing Provisions Section 5 prescriptive wall scope and requires the applicable NCC pathway.

cad.pattern: Bonded masonry with selected cores and joints carrying reinforcement and grout
cad.placement: On designed reinforced concrete support with bar continuity as detailed
cad.opening: Reinforcement and lintel or bond-beam details frame openings
cad.load: Designed reinforced structural wall

notes: Included for whole-building coverage, but detailed reinforced-masonry design is not inferred from Housing Provisions Section 5.

objects.name: isolated masonry pier
objects.definition: A freestanding vertical masonry support built from bonded units, separate from a continuous wall and used to carry a concentrated building load.
functions: Support a bearer, beam or other concentrated load
Transfer the supported load to a footing
Provide a durable discrete substructure support

ncc_references.relationship: Primary prescriptive context for isolated masonry piers.

cad.pattern: Discrete supports at bearer, beam or concentrated-load locations
cad.placement: Between an individual footing and the supported member
cad.load: Concentrated vertical support with restraint and tie-down as detailed

objects.name: subfloor masonry pier
objects.definition: An isolated masonry pier located beneath a suspended floor to support a bearer, beam or other floor-framing member above the ground.
functions: Support suspended floor framing
Maintain the floor above the subfloor space
Transfer floor and building loads to an individual footing

ncc_references.relationship: Subfloor application of an isolated masonry pier.

cad.pattern: Repeated support grid under suspended floor bearers
cad.placement: Within the subfloor between pad footing and bearer
cad.load: Suspended-floor support

objects.name: engaged masonry pier
objects.definition: A pier bonded integrally into a masonry wall so it projects from and locally stiffens the wall rather than standing as a separate isolated support.
functions: Locally stiffen a masonry wall
Increase the wall section at selected locations
Provide a bonded return-like projection within a single wall assembly

ncc_references.relationship: Wall-stiffening component in applicable single-leaf masonry construction.

cad.pattern: Vertical projections bonded into the wall at designed locations
cad.placement: Integral with one face or end of a masonry wall
cad.opening: Located relative to wall panels and openings as designed
cad.load: Local wall stiffening; not equivalent to an isolated column

notes: The National Dictionary distinction is retained: an engaged pier is integral with a wall, unlike an isolated pier.

objects.name: masonry wall panel
objects.definition: A continuous portion of masonry wall bounded by wall ends, returns, intersections, openings or movement joints and treated as one geometric and structural wall segment.
functions: Divide a long wall into modelled segments
Provide a host for units, joints and openings
Represent the wall length between articulation boundaries

cad.pattern: One segment between geometric or movement boundaries
cad.placement: Within a masonry wall run
cad.start: Wall end, return, opening boundary or articulation joint
cad.end: Wall end, return, opening boundary or articulation joint
cad.opening: May contain one or more supported openings
cad.load: Inherits the structural role of its wall arrangement

notes: This is a useful modelling subassembly, not a claim that the wall was prefabricated as a panel.

objects.name: masonry leaf
objects.definition: One continuous thickness of bonded masonry units within a wall, such as the single leaf of a veneer or one of the two leaves in a cavity wall.
functions: Form a continuous masonry plane
Carry its own weight and any assigned loads
Provide one side of a veneer, single-leaf or cavity wall arrangement

cad.pattern: Bonded units laid in repeated courses
cad.placement: At the modelled plane of a masonry wall leaf
cad.opening: Units are cut or omitted and supported around openings
cad.load: Depends on veneer, inner-leaf, outer-leaf or single-leaf role

objects.name: outer masonry leaf
objects.definition: The masonry leaf on the exterior side of a cavity masonry wall, exposed to outside weather and separated from the inner leaf by the cavity.
functions: Form the external masonry face
Receive and shed weather exposure
Transfer face loads to the inner leaf through cavity ties

cad.pattern: External bonded unit plane
cad.placement: Outside the cavity
cad.opening: Weather-detailed at heads, jambs and sills
cad.load: Exterior leaf; vertical and face-load role depends on design

objects.name: inner masonry leaf
objects.definition: The masonry leaf on the building-interior side of a cavity masonry wall, separated from the outer leaf by the cavity and commonly used as the structurally supporting leaf.
functions: Form the inner side of a cavity wall
Carry assigned roof, floor or wall loads where designed
Receive face loads transferred through cavity ties

cad.pattern: Internal bonded unit plane
cad.placement: Inside the cavity
cad.opening: Structurally supported around openings
cad.load: Commonly a loadbearing leaf; design governs

objects.name: masonry wall cavity
objects.definition: The intentional clear vertical space between a masonry leaf and another leaf or framed backing, kept sufficiently open to separate materials and allow moisture drainage.
functions: Interrupt direct moisture transfer across the wall
Provide drainage space behind the outer masonry
Separate leaves or separate veneer from its structural backing

cad.pattern: Continuous void behind or between masonry leaves
cad.placement: Between veneer and frame or between inner and outer masonry leaves
cad.opening: Maintained and detailed around doors, windows and penetrations
cad.load: Non-structural void crossed only by designed ties and accessories

notes: A cavity is modelled as physical negative space because its width, continuity and obstructions matter to drawing and checking tools.

objects.name: masonry course
objects.definition: A horizontal row of masonry units laid to a common level and bonded to the courses above and below with mortar joints.
functions: Organise units into repeated horizontal rows
Establish vertical wall set-out
Carry bonded loads through the wall thickness and height

cad.pattern: Repeated horizontal row with bond offset to adjacent courses
cad.placement: Within a masonry leaf
cad.opening: Interrupted or cut around openings and penetrations
cad.load: Horizontal unit row within the wall load path

objects.name: masonry unit
objects.definition: A preformed brick-, block- or stone-like component made to be laid with other units in bonded masonry construction.
functions: Provide the repeated solid body of a masonry wall
Bond with adjacent units through mortar
Carry compression and other assigned actions through the wall

cad.pattern: Repeated to a bond pattern in courses
cad.placement: Within a masonry leaf on a mortar bed
cad.opening: Cut, omitted or replaced by special units around openings
cad.load: Discrete compression-bearing masonry component

notes: Brick and block overlap in ordinary usage; tools should store actual dimensions and material rather than infer them from the short name alone.

objects.name: clay brick
objects.definition: A brick-sized fired clay masonry unit used in bonded brickwork for structural, veneer or facing applications.
functions: Form bonded brick masonry
Provide a durable facing surface where selected
Carry assigned masonry loads

cad.pattern: Repeated in bonded brick courses
cad.placement: Within a masonry leaf
cad.opening: Cut or omitted at openings
cad.load: Masonry unit role depends on wall arrangement

objects.name: calcium silicate brick
objects.definition: A brick-sized masonry unit manufactured principally from calcium-bearing and siliceous materials and used as a distinct brick material category.
functions: Form bonded masonry courses
Provide a selected masonry face and material performance
Carry assigned masonry loads

cad.pattern: Repeated in bonded courses
cad.placement: Within a masonry leaf
cad.opening: Cut or omitted at openings
cad.load: Masonry unit role depends on wall arrangement

objects.name: concrete brick
objects.definition: A brick-sized concrete masonry unit intended for uses similar to clay brick while retaining concrete as its material category.
functions: Form bonded brick-sized masonry
Provide a concrete masonry face
Carry assigned wall loads

cad.pattern: Repeated in bonded brick courses
cad.placement: Within a masonry leaf
cad.opening: Cut or omitted at openings
cad.load: Masonry unit role depends on wall arrangement

notes: Concrete brick and concrete block remain separate preferred objects because their modular sizes and common detailing differ, despite material overlap.

objects.name: concrete masonry block
objects.definition: A block-sized concrete masonry unit, commonly hollow, laid in bonded courses and capable of receiving grout and reinforcement where the system is designed for it.
functions: Form blockwork walls and piers
Provide hollow cores where applicable for services, grout or reinforcement
Carry assigned masonry loads

cad.pattern: Repeated in block courses with bond offset
cad.placement: Within a blockwork leaf or pier
cad.opening: Cut, omitted or replaced by special blocks
cad.load: Masonry unit; cores may participate in reinforced construction when filled

notes: Besser is retained only as a proprietary search term, never as the generic canonical name.

objects.name: solid masonry unit
objects.definition: A masonry unit without cores, although it may have small surface recesses, intended to be supported on mortar across its full bed area.
functions: Provide a substantially solid unit body
Transfer load through full mortar bedding
Represent draw-relevant unit geometry without internal cores

cad.pattern: Repeated according to masonry bond
cad.placement: On a full mortar bed within a course
cad.opening: Cut as detailed
cad.load: Full-bed masonry unit

notes: Unit form is independent of material; an instance may be both a clay brick and a solid masonry unit.

objects.name: cored masonry unit
objects.definition: A masonry unit containing vertical cores while still intended to be supported on mortar across the full bed area.
functions: Reduce unit mass or provide internal voids
Maintain full-bed mortar support
Represent vertical core geometry for detailing and quantity work

cad.pattern: Repeated with vertical cores aligned to unit orientation
cad.placement: On a full mortar bed within a course
cad.opening: Cut only where the product and detail permit
cad.load: Full-bed cored masonry unit

objects.name: hollow masonry unit
objects.definition: A masonry unit with vertical cores and distinct face shells, normally laid with mortar under the face shells rather than across the entire plan area.
functions: Form hollow block masonry
Provide cells that may remain empty or receive grout and reinforcement
Transfer load through face-shell bedding

cad.pattern: Repeated with vertically aligned or bonded cells
cad.placement: On face-shell mortar beds within blockwork
cad.opening: Special or cut units used as detailed
cad.load: Hollow unit whose cells may form part of reinforced construction

notes: Hollow and cored are not interchangeable classifications in the cited Australian terminology because their bedding differs.

objects.name: horizontally cored masonry unit
objects.definition: A masonry unit made with cores that run horizontally when the unit is placed in its intended laying orientation.
functions: Provide a specialised cored unit geometry
Form bonded masonry with horizontal internal voids
Retain the correct orientation for drawing and placement

cad.pattern: Repeated with core axes following the wall course
cad.placement: In the manufacturer's intended horizontal laying orientation
cad.opening: Cut only where permitted by the unit system
cad.load: Specialised full-bed masonry unit

objects.name: masonry mortar
objects.definition: A workable cementitious mixture placed between masonry units that hardens to bond them together, distribute contact and form the visible joints.
functions: Bond adjacent masonry units
Provide an even bearing bed between units
Seal and finish the joints at masonry faces

cad.pattern: Continuous bed strips and repeated vertical joints
cad.placement: Between adjacent masonry units
cad.opening: Omitted from deliberate weephole perpends and other specified openings
cad.load: Bonding and bearing material within masonry

notes: Mix selection is project- and exposure-dependent; the ontology records the material and classification fields, not a universal recipe.

objects.name: thin-bed masonry mortar
objects.definition: A proprietary masonry bonding material intended to be placed in a much thinner joint than conventional masonry mortar as part of a compatible unit system.
functions: Bond compatible precision masonry units
Form controlled thin horizontal and vertical joints
Reduce joint thickness within the proprietary system

cad.pattern: Thin continuous bonding layers between compatible units
cad.placement: At bed and perpend interfaces of the proprietary masonry system
cad.opening: Omitted where the system requires drainage openings
cad.load: Bonding layer within a compatible system

notes: Do not substitute thin-bed mortar for conventional mortar merely by changing joint thickness in the model.

objects.name: masonry bed joint
objects.definition: The horizontal mortar joint between one masonry course and the course immediately above or below it.
functions: Provide horizontal bedding and bond
Distribute bearing between courses
Establish the repeated vertical module of the masonry

cad.pattern: Continuous horizontal joint at each course level
cad.placement: Between stacked masonry courses
cad.opening: Interrupted by openings and some embedded components
cad.load: Horizontal bearing and bond joint

objects.name: masonry perpend
objects.definition: The vertical mortar joint between adjacent masonry units in the same course.
functions: Bond adjacent units within a course
Close the vertical gap between units
Complete the face and weather joint except where deliberately left open

cad.pattern: Repeated vertical joints between adjacent units with bond offset by course
cad.placement: Between units in the same masonry course
cad.opening: May intentionally remain open where it forms a weephole
cad.load: Vertical bonding joint rather than primary bearing bed

notes: A weephole may occupy an open perpend location, but an ordinary filled perpend is not a weephole.

objects.name: masonry core fill
objects.definition: Concrete, grout or mortar placed into selected hollow masonry cores so the filled cells become solid and can support reinforcement or improve the pier or wall section as designed.
functions: Fill selected unit cores
Surround and bond reinforcement where applicable
Create solid zones in piers or reinforced walls

cad.pattern: Vertical filled cell volumes at selected unit cores
cad.placement: Inside hollow masonry units
cad.opening: Flows around reinforcement and internal webs as the unit permits
cad.load: Solid core material acting with masonry and reinforcement as designed

notes: Core fill is a material volume, not the hollow core itself.

objects.name: masonry reinforcement
objects.definition: Steel bars or purpose-designed reinforcement placed in grouted masonry cores or mortar joints to strengthen a masonry assembly.
functions: Provide tensile and shear resistance to reinforced masonry
Connect reinforced masonry to supporting concrete where detailed
Strengthen selected cores, bond beams or joints

cad.pattern: Vertical bars in selected cores and horizontal reinforcement at detailed levels
cad.placement: Within grouted cores, bond beams or qualifying mortar joints
cad.opening: Detailed around openings and wall ends
cad.load: Structural reinforcement acting with masonry

notes: Accessories that do not qualify as structural reinforcement must not be promoted to this object merely because they are embedded in a bed joint.

objects.name: masonry bed-joint reinforcement
objects.definition: Purpose-designed steel reinforcement embedded horizontally in selected mortar bed joints to strengthen the masonry where the structural design recognises it as reinforcement.
functions: Provide horizontal reinforcement within masonry
Distribute local tensile forces or control cracking where designed
Connect reinforced regions across a bed joint

cad.pattern: Horizontal runs at selected bed-joint levels
cad.placement: Embedded centrally or as detailed in mortar bed joints
cad.opening: Interrupted or detailed around openings and movement joints
cad.load: Structural only when recognised by the applicable masonry design

notes: The term is deliberately narrower than any mesh accessory placed in a joint.

objects.name: masonry wall tie
objects.definition: A shaped metal wire or strap built into masonry to connect two cavity-wall leaves or connect a masonry veneer leaf to its structural backing.
functions: Transfer face loads between connected wall elements
Restrain a masonry leaf out of plane
Accommodate permitted differential movement according to tie type

ncc_references.relationship: Selection and placement context for wall ties in masonry veneer and cavity masonry.

cad.pattern: Repeated connector grid with extra ties around openings and edges as detailed
cad.placement: Crossing a cavity from the masonry leaf to another leaf or structural backing
cad.start: Embedded or fixed at first connected element
cad.end: Embedded or fixed at second connected element
cad.opening: Additional and repositioned ties occur near openings
cad.load: Face-load connector, not a vertical bearing support

notes: Tie class, duty and durability are attributes; cavity and veneer tie roles are separate child objects.

objects.name: masonry veneer wall tie
objects.definition: A wall tie that connects a single masonry veneer leaf to a timber, steel or masonry structural backing so face loads pass to that backing.
functions: Restrain masonry veneer against face loads
Connect veneer to its structural backing
Allow the differential movement required by the selected tie system

ncc_references.relationship: Wall-tie role connecting masonry veneer to structural backing.

cad.pattern: Repeated from frame members into veneer bed joints
cad.placement: Across the veneer cavity
cad.start: Fixed to structural frame or backing
cad.opening: Additional tie layout follows opening edges
cad.load: Transfers veneer face load to structural backing

objects.name: cavity wall tie
objects.definition: A wall tie embedded into both masonry leaves of a cavity wall to transfer face loads between the inner and outer leaves.
functions: Connect inner and outer masonry leaves
Transfer face loads between leaves
Maintain structural restraint while allowing specified differential movement

ncc_references.relationship: Wall-tie role connecting two masonry leaves.

cad.pattern: Repeated across the cavity at masonry bed-joint levels
cad.placement: Between inner and outer masonry leaves
cad.opening: Additional tie layout follows opening edges
cad.load: Transfers face loads between masonry leaves

objects.name: masonry wall-tie fixing
objects.definition: The screw, nail, clip or anchor that secures a veneer wall tie to its structural frame or backing where the tie is not built directly into masonry at both ends.
functions: Fasten a veneer tie to structural backing
Transfer tie force into the frame or backing
Complete the tested or specified tie-and-fixing system

cad.pattern: One compatible fixing at each frame-fixed tie end
cad.placement: Through the tie attachment into structural backing
cad.load: Transfers wall-tie force to backing

notes: The tie and its fixing are separately selectable physical objects even where sold as one system.

objects.name: steel masonry lintel
objects.definition: A horizontal steel member built into masonry over a door, window or other opening to support the masonry and any assigned loads above the opening.
functions: Span a masonry opening
Support masonry above the opening
Transfer supported loads to masonry bearings at each end

ncc_references.relationship: Steel-lintel object and corrosion-protection context for masonry openings.

cad.pattern: One or more members at each applicable masonry opening
cad.placement: Directly beneath supported masonry over the opening
cad.start: Bearing on masonry at one jamb
cad.end: Bearing on masonry at opposite jamb
cad.opening: Spans the clear opening and any required cavity or leaf width
cad.load: Beam supporting masonry and assigned loads above an opening

notes: Lintel geometry and capacity must be selected from the applicable design or schedule, not inferred from opening width alone.

objects.name: angle masonry lintel
objects.definition: A steel masonry lintel formed from an angle section, with one leg supporting the masonry bed and the other providing section depth and restraint.
functions: Support a masonry leaf over an opening
Provide a compact edge support at the masonry bed
Transfer lintel reactions to end bearings

ncc_references.relationship: Recognised steel-lintel section form.

cad.pattern: One angle member per supported leaf or as scheduled
cad.placement: At the head of a masonry opening
cad.opening: Spans across the opening
cad.load: Angle-section lintel

objects.name: flat-bar masonry lintel
objects.definition: A steel masonry lintel formed from a flat rectangular bar placed beneath and supporting the masonry over an opening.
functions: Support masonry over a limited opening where suitable
Provide a concealed horizontal bearing strip
Transfer supported masonry load to end bearings

ncc_references.relationship: Recognised steel-lintel section form.

cad.pattern: One flat member per supported leaf or as scheduled
cad.placement: At the head of a masonry opening
cad.opening: Spans across the opening
cad.load: Flat-section lintel

objects.name: masonry fixing strap
objects.definition: A metal strap built into masonry and fixed to adjacent framing or another building element to provide restraint or connection at that interface.
functions: Connect framing to masonry
Restrain connected elements against separation or movement
Transfer specified connection forces into built-in masonry embedment

ncc_references.relationship: Fixing-strap and tie-down component context.

cad.pattern: Repeated at specified frame-to-masonry connection locations
cad.placement: Built into a mortar joint or masonry core and fixed to the connected frame
cad.opening: May occur at jambs and other opening interfaces
cad.load: Connection and restraint strap

objects.name: masonry roof tie-down strap
objects.definition: A metal strap built into or anchored through masonry and connected to roof framing so uplift forces can pass from the roof into the supporting wall and foundation load path.
functions: Restrain roof framing against uplift
Connect roof framing to masonry
Continue the tie-down load path through the wall support

ncc_references.relationship: Roof tie-down strap context for masonry construction.

cad.pattern: At roof-framing tie-down points
cad.placement: From built-in masonry anchorage to truss, rafter, plate or other roof member
cad.opening: Routed clear of openings unless specifically detailed
cad.load: Tension connector in roof uplift load path

objects.name: masonry tie-down rod
objects.definition: A steel rod passing through or beside masonry and anchored to the footing or lower structure to provide a continuous tensile tie-down connection to framing above.
functions: Carry tie-down tension through the masonry height
Connect supported framing to the footing or lower anchor
Provide a continuous uplift load path

ncc_references.relationship: Vertical rod used in applicable pier and masonry tie-down arrangements.

cad.pattern: One at each detailed tie-down point
cad.placement: Vertically through a masonry core or formed path
cad.end: Upper framing washer, plate or connector
cad.opening: Requires a continuous clear or formed path through the masonry
cad.load: Tension tie-down member

objects.name: masonry damp-proof course
objects.definition: A continuous moisture-resistant layer built into a masonry wall to interrupt capillary moisture rising or passing through the wall at the selected level.
functions: Interrupt rising damp through masonry
Separate masonry from moisture-sensitive construction
Form part of a combined flashing or termite-management detail where the product is suitable

ncc_references.relationship: Damp-proof course material and placement context for masonry.

cad.pattern: Continuous strip through the wall or leaf at the selected course
cad.placement: At wall bases and other required damp-interruption levels
cad.opening: Lapped and turned to maintain continuity around junctions
cad.load: Moisture-control layer with negligible structural capacity

notes: DPC and flashing can use the same sheet product but remain separate functional roles in the ontology.

objects.name: masonry flashing
objects.definition: A shaped moisture-resistant sheet built into a masonry wall to collect water from a cavity or exposed interface and direct it to the outside through an edge or weepholes.
functions: Collect incidental water within masonry construction
Direct water outward
Protect wall interfaces, openings and supports from retained moisture

ncc_references.relationship: Flashing material, location and drainage context for masonry.

cad.pattern: Continuous or locally tray-shaped sheet at moisture collection points
cad.placement: At wall bases, above supports and around openings
cad.end: External discharge edge or sealed end
cad.opening: Wrapped, lapped or tray-formed around openings and penetrations
cad.load: Moisture-drainage component

notes: Flashing geometry should be modelled as a water path, not just a material tag on one course.

objects.name: masonry sill flashing
objects.definition: A flashing tray or strip at the sill of a wall opening that collects water at the lower opening interface and directs it toward the exterior drainage path.
functions: Protect the wall below an opening
Collect water at the sill interface
Drain water to the outer face or cavity outlets

ncc_references.relationship: Flashing role at the sill of masonry wall openings.

cad.pattern: One tray or strip at each applicable opening sill
cad.placement: Below the sill and extending to the drainage face
cad.opening: Follows the sill width and integrates with jamb and frame details
cad.load: Moisture collection and drainage only

objects.name: masonry head flashing
objects.definition: A flashing installed above a wall opening to intercept water descending through the masonry or cavity and discharge it outward before it reaches the opening head.
functions: Intercept water above an opening
Protect the lintel, frame head and interior
Direct collected water to external outlets or weepholes

ncc_references.relationship: Flashing role at the head of masonry wall openings.

cad.pattern: One tray or strip above each applicable opening
cad.placement: Above the lintel or opening head with an external discharge path
cad.opening: Spans beyond the opening and integrates with cavity drainage
cad.load: Moisture collection and drainage only

objects.name: masonry weephole
objects.definition: A deliberate open gap, commonly occupying a perpend above flashing or at the bottom of a cavity, that lets collected water drain to the outside.
functions: Drain water from flashing and cavity zones
Vent the immediate cavity opening where the detail permits
Make the wall drainage outlet visible and model-checkable
materials: optional formed insert or screen where specified

objects.name: vertical masonry articulation joint

objects.name: flexible masonry joint sealant
